answer: Give every identity a terrace of trust tiers, climbed only through verified useful work for strangers — no buying a rung. A hollow identity that just registered sits on the lowest terrace, where it may only read and post; real earning power unlocks rung by rung as established peers attest its work. Cloning then costs full labor per identity: ten thousand fakes each have to climb from the basement themselves. Falcon-fast onboarding exists, but only when two already-established, non-kin sponsors stake collateral on the newcomer — and they lose the stake if it turns out to be a sock puppet.
